newsitem.title: GERMANY: Deutsche's Kopper sees EMU boosting jobs, growth.
newsitem.headline: Deutsche's Kopper sees EMU boosting jobs, growth.

text.p: Deutsche Bank AG supervisory board chairman Hilmar Kopper said on Tuesday Europe's planned single currency should promote growth and jobs in the European Union region.

Addressing the Global 24 European monetary union conference, Kopper said the euro would smooth out competitive differences between European businesses and their counterparts in the U.S. and Japan, which had long benefited from economies of scale.
He also said it would be "dangerous and extremely counter-productive" to start an official debate on postponing the euro launch.

"By eliminating exchange rate fluctuations and currency-related exchange rate costs, Europe will achieve a genuine single market," said Kopper, the former management board chairman at Germany's largest commercial bank. "Increased competition, the reduction of exchange rate risks and costs and growing international competitiveness will stimulate economic growth in the European private sector."
Kopper said countries would be forced to focus on structural policies once issues on exchange rates and monetary policies had been taken away from governments.
"This means tax reform, deregulation and flexibility of product and labour markets. Eventually, this could also pave the way for higher employment, which is urgently needed."
Kopper said failure to launch the euro on time would have damaging consequences.

"A failure of EMU would initially entail major unrest on the currency markets, probably resulting in a pronounced revaluation of the deutschemark and an increase in interest rates in partner countries with depreciating currencies," he said.
Kopper said fiscal policies in Germany and France presented the main risk to a punctual EMU start.
"Germany can still meet the three-percent target even though a higher figure seems to be more likely at this point in time," he said.
